## Scope

- Source Issue / Runbook:
- Verified base SHA / exact review head:
- Changed files and reasons:
- Standard book / target / edition / legacy boundary:
- Compatibility / rollback / excluded work:

## Verification evidence

Record command, environment and result; N/A needs a reason. Do not check an
unexecuted gate or equate a build plan with a deployable book.

- [ ] Root install/audit/test/lint/build/Node24 Actions / diff check
- [ ] Standard-book schema / source visibility / Markdown CLI gates
- [ ] Target-specific generated artifact / leakage / links / browser gates (or N/A)
- [ ] Exact-head CI run URLs / IDs
- [ ] Known warnings, excluded suites, skips and follow-up Issues recorded
- [ ] No private/paid content, secret or credential in public evidence

## Review and completion

- [ ] Independent review at the exact current head
- [ ] Every review body / inline / suggestion / suppressed item / thread disposition
- [ ] Unresolved / count mismatch / missing review IDs: 0 / 0 / 0
- [ ] Ready-transition automatic review completed where configured
- [ ] Normal merge authorized by task; no bypass / force / direct main push
- [ ] Merge SHA and main CI / CodeQL findings checked separately from npm audit
- [ ] Consumer Pages/deployment / public HTTP/marker / desktop/mobile (or N/A)
- [ ] Source Issue DoD and owned cleanup complete

See [the common workflow](https://github.com/itdojp/book-formatter/blob/main/docs/codex-cli-workflow.md). Consumer mutation and
public rollout require their own audited SHA, clean worktree, allowlist and
review; a formatter merge does not deploy any consumer automatically.
